A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2D research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–B. Inspection supports matching retained, relocated, added and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original JailbreakBench and HarmBench experiments, XSTest over-refusal measurements, and CPO/pivot ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds general-ability evaluations and reasoning-model experiments with training, prompting and inference controls in Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The SwaRD procedure, pivot tagging and CPO objective are retained. v2 introduces R2D-ZeroThink (Table 3), which concludes reasoning during inference and produces short responses, adding a limited inference variant. Applying the existing training method to additional reasoning models does not establish an architectural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual general-ability evaluations on ARC-E, ARC-C, BoolQ, MMLU, MMLU STEM, PIQA and SciQ (Table 2), extending measured coverage beyond safety and refusal into knowledge, question answering and reasoning. v1 mentions general-dataset evaluation but supplies no corresponding results. Alpaca/AdvBench training and JailbreakBench, HarmBench and XSTest evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Safety-tuned Llamas as an evaluated training-based defense across three attacks and six base models; v1 only discusses it as related work. Table 3 also introduces the prompt-only R2D-p comparator. The existing filtering and external-defense baselines remain, while None is renamed Vanilla.

E3.justification: v1 evaluates unmodified QwQ-preview-32B and DeepSeek-R1-70B; v2 instead evaluates QwQ-32B and R1-7B/32B with matched Vanilla, R2D, prompting and ZeroThink conditions. R1-70B remains the trajectory teacher. v2 adds accuracy evaluation through lm-evaluation-harness and response word counts, while reducing the reported XSTest model set from six to three. Existing training defaults and safety judges remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 3 tests training versus prompt-only safety and the effects of curtailing reasoning on safety and response length. Conversely, v2 removes the Llama-3-8B and Vicuna-7B/13B XSTest analyses under both judges. The remaining Dic-Judge results move to Appendix A.3. Original CPO/pivot ablations and Appendix B success/failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 newly reports response word counts with ± quantities, such as 884±789 for vanilla R1-7B. The statistic represented by ± is undefined. Neither version documents repeated-run counts, seeds or ASR confidence intervals, so this addition does not establish additional runs or significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 adds capability, reasoning-model, response-length and Safety-tuned Llamas results, and removes Llama/Vicuna XSTest entries. Figure 3 revises original Llama-3-8B ASRs from 29%, 28%, 37%, 32% to 9%, 2%, 9%, 5% for ZeroShot, FewShot, PAIR and AutoDAN respectively; its R2D values remain unchanged. Retained non-reasoning JailbreakBench and CPO-ablation scores are unchanged. The new reasoning-model scores concern different model configurations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The trajectory construction, SwaRD objective, probability factorization and CPO formulation in Equations 1–4 are unchanged, as is the ASR definition in Equation 5. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations appear in v2 or its appendices.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly extends the abstract and conclusion to improving already-reasoning LRMs alongside ordinary LLMs. The central SwaRD/CPO defense contribution and avoidance-of-over-refusal claim remain. General-performance preservation receives greater prominence in the abstract and conclusion, but was already asserted in v1's introduction.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new controls as evidence of safety beyond prompting and safety persisting without extended reasoning. It removes v1's qualification that Llama/Vicuna become prone to over-refusal and the proposed pretraining-data explanation, plus the small-model caveat to baseline superiority. New capability results are interpreted as essentially preserving performance. The standalone Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 identifies and links lm-evaluation-harness for capability testing and documents the revised reasoning-model choices in Appendix A.2. The synthesis prompt, sample counts, LoRA hyperparameters, hardware and code-access statement remain. v2 omits v1's explicit description of hiding [UNSAFE] reasoning and answers; whether the implementation changed is unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds SafeChain (Jiang et al., 2025) to the reasoning-safety discussion and Qi et al. (2025) on safety-alignment depth. The QwQ reference changes from the 2024 preview release to the 2025 QwQ-32B release. The broader positioning of internal safety reasoning relative to guardrails and refusal training remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, opening introduction and framework overview are reworded, LRM terminology and an equal-contribution note are introduced, and the Models description moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix A.2. Discussion headings are revised. The main section sequence, training exposition, limitations and case-study prose remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 restructures Table 1 by removing reasoning-model columns and adding baseline rows, and introduces two substantial results tables. Figure 3 changes from a 2-by-2 arrangement to four panels in one row. The XSTest display is reduced and split between main-text Figure 4 and appendix Figure 5, with revised legends and spacing. Figures 1–2 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: New capability measurements and training/prompting controls address important evidential gaps in v1. However, v2 removes adverse Llama/Vicuna XSTest results and their qualification while retaining the blanket no-over-refusal conclusion. Its conclusion also asserts no performance drops despite decreases in Table 2, such as R1-32B ARC-C from 61.35 to 57.08 after R2D. Broader evaluation and less balanced reporting are both material, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
